title: SaaS cash runway: what fills and drains the bank balance
caption: Structural model of a Series-A SaaS company's monthly cash dynamics; rates illustrative, USD/month.

semantic_description.level_1_elemental: A stock-and-flow diagram with two stocks: Cash Position (rectangle, initial 4.2M USD) and Active Customers (850 accounts). Cash is filled by the Revenue Collected inflow from a source cloud and drained by the Operating Spend outflow to a sink cloud. Active Customers is filled by New Wins from a prospect cloud and drained by Churned to a lost cloud. Eight dashed information links feed auxiliaries (ARPA, churn rate, win rate, qualified leads, CAC, S&M spend, headcount cost, runway) into the flow valves.
semantic_description.level_2_statistical: Inflow rate = active_customers * ARPA = 850 * 1450 = 1.2325M USD/month. Outflow rate = headcount (610k) + S&M (320k) = 930k USD/month. Net cash change is +303k/month at the initial point, so the runway auxiliary is positive (not burning) at t0; the model tips to burn only if customers fall below ~641 or ARPA drops.
semantic_description.level_3_perceptual: Two parallel conveyor structures stacked vertically: a money loop on top and a customer loop below, linked because Active Customers drives the Revenue Collected valve. The auxiliary cloud on the right (S&M spend) fans out to three valves at once, making it the highest-leverage control point.
semantic_description.level_4_contextual: The structure shows why cutting S&M to extend runway is self-defeating: it simultaneously starves the lead engine that feeds New Wins, shrinking the customer base that drives Revenue Collected.
semantic_description.short_alt: Stock-and-flow model: Cash filled by revenue, drained by spend; Customers filled by wins, drained by churn; spend drives both.
